title: Requisition-to-Ramp: Hiring Velocity and Budget Approval Runbook
author: Aisha Gupta
body:
Summary

This runbook describes the standardized end-to-end process from role requisition through new-hire ramp (the "requisition-to-ramp" lifecycle). It focuses on: hiring velocity targets, budget and headcount approval gates, manager responsibilities at each phase, and operational playbooks to reduce time-to-ramp while preserving hiring quality and compliance. Use this page as the canonical process for all full-time and contractor requisitions unless a business exception is granted by People Ops.

Scope and goals

- Scope: all US/EMEA/APAC salaried roles and contractor requisitions initiated by Redwood teams. Excludes executive hires, mergers & acquisitions, and externally managed vendor hiring (see related policies).
- Goals:
  - Median time from approved requisition to offer accepted: <= 35 calendar days (target).
  - Median time from offer accepted to first meaningful contribution (ramp): 60 calendar days for IC1-IC3 roles; 45 calendar days for contractor/short-term ICs.
  - Maintain interview quality: >= 85% hiring manager satisfaction (post-hire survey).
  - Ensure budget compliance: < 2% of hires made outside approved headcount pool per quarter.

Quick reference: phase owners and SLAs

- Phase 1: Requisition Intake & Prioritization — owner: Hiring Manager + People Ops intake. SLA: 3 business days to decision (approve / defer / reject).
- Phase 2: Job Profile & Panel Setup — owner: Hiring Manager + Recruiter. SLA: 5 business days to publish job and assemble panel.
- Phase 3: Interviewing & Debrief — owner: Recruiting + Interview Panel. SLA: first round within 10 business days of posting.
- Phase 4: Offer Approval & Budget Signoff — owner: Hiring Manager + Finance + People Ops. SLA: 2 business days for standard approvals.
- Phase 5: Offer Presentation to Candidate — owner: Recruiter. SLA: within 24 hours of approval.
- Phase 6: Onboarding & Ramp Tracking — owner: Manager + People Ops. SLA: onboarding checklist completed by day 7; first 30/60/90 check-ins scheduled at hire.

Approval gates and decision rules

Every requisition flows through the following discrete gates. If a gate is not satisfied, the requisition must be paused and recorded in the Hiring Intake tracker with the reason and next action date.

1) Budget Gate (pre-search):
   - Required artifacts: approved headcount CSV row or signed budget request form; justification memo (200–400 words) describing ROI and urgency.
   - Approvers: hiring manager, finance approver (cost center owner), People Ops lead for the org.
   - Decision options: Approved / Deferred / Redirect to contractor pool.

2) Role Readiness Gate (job readiness & candidate profile):
   - Required artifacts: finalized job profile (capabilities + success metrics), scorecard (minimum pass/fail criteria), interview rubric draft.
   - Approvers: hiring manager and assigned recruiter.

3) Final Offer Gate (comp & package signoff):
   - Required artifacts: proposed OTE/comp package, equity recommendation (if applicable), start date window, relocation/visa budget if needed.
   - Approvers: hiring manager, People Ops compensation partner, Finance (if exceeds comp band).

4) Ramp & Performance Gate (post-hire):
   - Required artifacts: 30/60/90 plan uploaded to the HRIS, initial success metrics, mentor/peer pairings.
   - Approvers: hiring manager and People Ops onboarding partner.

Operational procedures (step-by-step)

A. Request creation (Day 0)
1. Hiring Manager opens a requisition in the Hiring Intake form and attaches budget artifacts.
2. People Ops triages and assigns a recruiter within 72 hours.
3. If budget is missing or out-of-cycle, People Ops returns the req with required next steps.

B. Job profile and panel setup (Day 1-7)
1. Recruiter drafts job posting from standard templates and circulates to manager for final edits (target: 48 hours).
2. Manager defines scorecard (3–5 core competencies + 1–2 role-specific deliverables).
3. Panel members invited; People Ops ensures at least one DEI-aware interviewer on each panel.

C. Interview scheduling and debriefs (Day 7-35)
1. Recruiter screens and schedules candidates in prioritized batches (minimum 3 candidates per active requisition).
2. Interviewers use the shared rubric and record scores in the interviewing tool.
3. Debrief within 24 hours of final interview; decisions recorded as Hire / No Hire / Hold.

D. Offer approval and negotiation (Day 35-45 target)
1. Hiring Manager completes the Offer Recommendation form with comp and equity.
2. People Ops and Compensation review; Finance signs off if outside band.
3. Recruiter extends offer and records acceptance in applicant tracking system.

E. Onboarding and ramp monitoring (Day 0-90 post start)
1. Manager uploads 30/60/90 plan and assigns mentor by Day 3.
2. People Ops triggers security, equipment, HRIS provisioning within 48 hours of accepted offer.
3. Running cadence: 30/60/90 milestone check-ins with standardized templates and pass/fail evidence.

Manager responsibilities checklist

- Pre-hire: craft job profile, define scorecard, secure leadership & finance alignment, nominate panel members.
- Interview phase: ensure timely interviewer calibration, provide feedback standardization, commit to debrief schedule.
- Offer phase: approve package promptly, provide clear rationale for exceptions.
- Post-hire: run 30/60/90 cadence, record ramp evidence, escalate coaching needs to People Ops if target milestones are not met.

Process accelerators and exceptions

- Fast-Track Hiring: for high-priority business-critical roles, request "fast-track" at intake. Fast-track requires Exec sponsor and reduces SLAs: intake decision within 24 hours, interviews within 5 business days, and immediate finance pre-approval. Use only sparingly (target < 5% of hires).
- Contractor-to-FTE conversion: follow separate conversion checklist (link to related page). Budget gate requires evidence of performance and hiring manager justification.
- International hires (visa/relocation): add 10 business days to standard timelines for visa approvals; secure immigration budget before posting.

Quality controls, metrics, and reporting

Key metrics to track weekly and quarterly:
- Time-to-offer (median days)
- Time-to-ramp (median days to defined "first meaningful contribution")
- Interview-to-offer ratio
- Offer acceptance rate
- Percent hires within approved headcount pool
- Hiring manager satisfaction (post-hire survey)

Reporting cadence and owners:
- Recruiting ops: weekly dashboard of open reqs, stage duration, and blockers.
- People Ops: monthly headcount and budget variance report to Finance.
- Hiring Managers: post-hire survey at 30 days; People Ops compiles quarterly calibration reviews.

Sample configuration table: approval routing (text table)

| Requisition size | Required approvers | Escalation after | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| New IC under band | Hiring Manager; People Ops | 3 business days | Auto-approved if budget row exists |
| Senior IC / Manager | Hiring Manager; Finance; People Ops | 2 business days | Finance reviews comp if > 10% of midpoint |
| Executive / Director | Hiring Manager; VP; Finance; People Ops; CEO notified | 1 business day | Exec sponsorship required |

Common failure modes and mitigations

- Failure: requisition stalls in Budget Gate. Mitigation: People Ops runs weekly "unstuck" office hours with Finance to resolve clarifications and propose temporary contractor coverage where justified.
- Failure: interview panel no-shows causing scheduling delays. Mitigation: enforce interview swap list and require panel confirmation 48 hours prior to scheduled interviews.
- Failure: candidate acceptance delays due to slow comp approvals. Mitigation: recruiters provision conditional offers (subject to final finance signoff) in urgent cases following fast-track guidelines.

Template artifacts and links (centralized)

- Requisition Intake form (HRIS link).
- Job profile template (Google Doc).
- Offer Recommendation form (internal).
- 30/60/90 plan template (HRIS attachments).
- Hiring intake tracker (shared spreadsheet).

Appendix: negotiation guardrails and comp bands

- Managers must consult the public comp band table before recommending offers. Requests above band require People Ops compensation review and Finance approval.
- Negotiation cushions: standard offer may include a buffer of up to 5% for base and 10% for joining bonuses within the band; anything larger requires explicit signoff.
